note: Recorded model answers, one per judgement call site. This is the honest part of the laptop path: no provider, no key, no GPU — the four judgement phases replay these, and the kernel validates each one exactly as it would validate a live model's answer.

verify.rationale: only model/structure.json changed; metric.mjs and the seeded data generator are untouched, so the comparison against the baseline stays honest

r1-h1.root_cause: the hidden layer can represent the interaction but recovers only part of it in the epochs it is given; capacity is the right direction and the wrong instrument

r1-h2.root_cause: the explicit cross gives the additive model the pairwise term it could not represent, which is where the metric's headroom was

r1-h3.root_cause: l2 changes the calibration of the fit and not its ranking, so auc lands back at the baseline

round_reflect.summary: the interaction hypothesis moved auc from 0.707 to 0.730 while extra capacity moved it to 0.718 and regularisation moved nothing. The headroom was representational, not parametric.

lessons.statement: when a prior names a pairwise interaction, making it explicit beats buying capacity to discover it
lessons.evidence: r1-h2 (0.730) against r1-h1 (0.718) for a fifth of the training time

lessons.statement: l2 is not a lever on a ranking metric in this space — it should not be proposed as one

next_round_focus: cross the second and third fields, which the priors do not yet say anything about
check whether the four crosses are enough or the interaction needs its own embedding
